一.meaning: A single stroke represents the concept of 'one' — it's the simplest beginning.
一.onyomi: Yusuf needed just one brushstroke to capture the essence of the desert sunset.
一.kunyomi: Ichi — 'itch' — that one little itch drove him crazy.

二.meaning: Two horizontal lines represent the duality of 'two' — a pair, a contrast.
二.onyomi: Sho caught two perfect waves, one after the other, in a row.
二.kunyomi: Rita — 'Re-ta' — two ta-da moments in one show.

九.meaning: A loop around a 'woman' radical — nine months to bring a new life into the world.
九.onyomi: Kyu was late to class again, rushing in with a frantic look.
九.kunyomi: Koko — 'co-co' — a small child's cooing sound.

七.meaning: A 'ten' with a 'gate' — seven days to open the gate to a new week.
七.onyomi: Shula demanded seven days of intense training to prepare the team.

人.meaning: A walking person, clearly showing a human figure — it’s the most basic depiction of a person.
人.onyomi: Khan led his army of people across the vast desert.
人.kunyomi: Hito — 'He toe' — he pointed his toe to show the way.

入.meaning: A 'person' stepping through a 'gate' — the action of entering a place.
入.onyomi: Rio entered the bustling marketplace, eager to explore.
入.kunyomi: Iri — 'Ee-ree' - 'Eee, ree!' he shouted as he ran in.

八.meaning: Eight droplets of water forming a circular pattern — like the eight points of a compass.
八.onyomi: Homer crashed his car, scattering eight droplets of water across the road.

十.meaning: A simple cross, representing the number 'ten' — a full count.
十.onyomi: Joe used his lockpicks to open ten doors in the warehouse.
十.kunyomi: Too — 'too' — he had too much to carry.

三.meaning: A 'ground' with two strokes above — three distinct elements combined.
三.onyomi: Sosa hit three home runs in a single game.
三.kunyomi: Mi — 'me' — he wanted to be like the great heroes.

上.meaning: A 'toe' above the 'ground' — representing something being higher or above.
上.onyomi: Kofi built the house on the upper level.

下.meaning: A person tripped and fell downwards — they're under something.
下.onyomi: Carlos quickly descended the stairs to greet his guests.
下.kunyomi: Shita — 'she ate' — she ate something that fell down.

大.meaning: A giant tree (木) stands tall, completely overshadowing a smaller tree — it’s big.
大.onyomi: Tova’s farm was the biggest in the county.
大.kunyomi: Ooya — 'oh yeah' — Oh yeah, that’s a big one!

女.meaning: A woman (亅) stands proudly beside a cloth (巾) — she’s dressed elegantly.
女.onyomi: Selma’s daughter, Jyo, was a beautiful dancer.
女.kunyomi: Onna — 'own nah' — ‘Own nah, I’m a woman!’

山.meaning: Three mountains (三) rise dramatically from the earth (土) — it's a mountain.
山.onyomi: Sosa hit the ball so hard it flew over the mountain.
山.kunyomi: Yama — 'yam' — a giant yam-shaped mountain blocking the road.

川.meaning: Water (氵) flows between two grassy banks (艹) — it’s a river.
川.onyomi: Senna raced across the bridge over the river.
川.kunyomi: Kawa — 'car wa' — the car was washed away in the river.

土.meaning: A mound of earth (土) is carefully placed, forming a solid base — it’s soil.
土.onyomi: Tay carefully inspected the soil for imperfections.
土.kunyomi: Tsuchi — 'too cheese' — ‘Too cheesy for the garden, it needs more soil!’

千.meaning: A thousand (千) sheets of paper (丨) are neatly stacked high — it’s a thousand.
千.onyomi: Senna aimed for a thousand laps around the track.
千.kunyomi: Chi — 'cheese' — a thousand slices of cheese!

子.meaning: A small child (小) clings to their parent (子) — it’s a child.
子.onyomi: Kay examined the child's fingerprints for clues.
子.kunyomi: Ko — 'cone' — a child eating a cone.

小.meaning: A small mouth (小) opens wide in surprise — it's small.
小.onyomi: Sho took a small bite of the pineapple.
小.kunyomi: Chii — 'cheesey' — this is a cheesey small snack.

中.meaning: A field (田) is enclosed within walls (回) — it’s in the middle.
中.onyomi: Kofi built a house in the middle of the forest.
中.kunyomi: Naka — 'nuke' — ‘Let’s go to the middle of the park.’

五.meaning: Five fingers splayed out – it’s a hand counting.
五.onyomi: Kofi used five planks of wood to build a new fence.
五.kunyomi: Go — 'glow' — the firelight gave off a warm glow.

六.meaning: Six fish swimming in a pond – a school of fish.
六.onyomi: Sosa hit six home runs in a single game.
六.kunyomi: Mu — 'mew' — a cat meows six times.

円.meaning: A lid (蓋) placed on a head (日) – a circular seal.
円.onyomi: The yen (円) is the currency of Japan.
円.kunyomi: Maru — 'marooned' — the ship was marooned in a circular bay.

天.meaning: A roof (宀) covering the heavens (日) – the sky above.
天.onyomi: Tova looked up at the sky and felt a connection to the heavens.
天.kunyomi: Amatsu — 'amass' — the rain amassed into a vast, grey sky.

日.meaning: The sun (日) shining brightly – it's a day!
日.onyomi: Nichiido, Japan's national holiday, celebrates the sun.
日.kunyomi: Hi — 'high' — the sun was high in the sky.

月.meaning: The moon (月) illuminating the night sky – a lunar glow.
月.onyomi: Gatsu – the August moon hangs heavy in the sky.
月.kunyomi: Tsuki — 'tuck' — she tucked herself into bed under the moonlight.

木.meaning: A tree (木) standing tall and proud – it's a forest.
木.onyomi: Boku used wood to build a small boat.
木.kunyomi: Ki — 'key' — the key to the forest was a single, old tree.

水.meaning: Water (水) flowing freely – a river’s gentle current.
水.onyomi: The suit (水) was soaked from the rain.
水.kunyomi: Mizu — 'me zoo' — a zoo full of animals drinking water.

火.meaning: Fire (火) burning brightly – a warm, cozy hearth.
火.onyomi: Ka-boom! The fireworks lit up the night sky.
火.kunyomi: Hi — 'high' — the flames reached high into the sky.

出.meaning: A mountain (出) emerging from the ground – a rise in the landscape.
出.onyomi: Shutsu – the shop’s exit was blocked by boxes.
出.kunyomi: De — 'dew' — the dew collected on the mountain slopes.

右.meaning: A narwhal's horn points to the right, indicating direction – it shows the way to the right.
右.kunyomi: Migi - 'my ghee' - I made a delicious spread with ghee on the right side of the table.

四.meaning: Four legs support a mouth – a creature standing proudly.
四.kunyomi: Yo - 'yoyo' - The yoyo fell down four times.

左.meaning: A narwhal's horn points to the left, indicating direction – it shows the way to the left.
左.kunyomi: Hidari - 'hi dairy' - The dairy farm is on the left side of the road.

本.meaning: A book resting on a table — a classic source of knowledge.
本.kunyomi: Moto - 'moat' - The castle’s moat protected the book of ancient secrets.

白.meaning: A white cloth covering something – it's pure and clean.
白.kunyomi: Shiro - 'she rowed' - She rowed the boat with a white sail.

万.meaning: A leaf covering a sword – it represents an abundance of power and potential.
万.kunyomi: Yorozu - 'your zoo' -  Your zoo has ten thousand different animals.

今.meaning: A mouth surrounded by a frame — it marks the present moment.
今.kunyomi: Ima - 'eye ma' - I saw my mom just now.

午.meaning: The sun slides across the sky at noon — it signifies midday.
午.kunyomi: Uma - 'oo ma' - The horse (uma) grazed at noon.

友.meaning: A narwhal’s horn resting on a stool – a sign of companionship and support.
友.kunyomi: Tomo - 'toe mo' -  Toe mo, I’ll always be your friend.

父.meaning: A father’s face is warm and comforting - he provides and protects.
父.kunyomi: Chichi - 'cheese cheese' - My dad loves cheese cheese!

北.meaning: Imagine a spoon (spoon radical) gently scooping up the northern wind, guiding it across the land.
北.onyomi: Homer tripped over a rock, shouting 'Hoku!' as he fell.
北.kunyomi: Kita – 'keeta' – a little kid who’s always pointing north.

半.meaning: A triceratops (triceratops radical) is split in half, representing just one side of a whole.
半.onyomi: Hans meticulously measured half a sheet of paper.
半.kunyomi: Naka - 'nacka' - a nack of half a cookie.

外.meaning: The evening (evening radical) light shines on a single toe (toe radical), marking the boundary of the known world.
外.onyomi: Gai, the guide, led them outside the city walls.
外.kunyomi: Soto - 'so-toe' - a toe sticking out of the door.

母.meaning: A drop (drop radical) of sunlight (sun radical) falls onto the earth, nourishing the mother figure.
母.onyomi: Bo, the police officer, said 'Bo!' to a child running into the street.
母.kunyomi: Haha – 'hah-ha' – a mother laughing at her child's antics.

休.meaning: A leader (leader radical) rests beneath the shade of a tree (tree radical), finally taking a break.
休.onyomi: Kyu, the student, was late to class again.
休.kunyomi: Yasu - 'yah-soo' - a yasu (easy) day of rest.

先.meaning: A slide (slide radical) leads to a patch of dirt (dirt radical), marking the path ahead.
先.onyomi: Senna raced ahead, taking the lead.

名.meaning: The evening (evening radical) light illuminates a mouth (mouth radical) as a name is spoken.
名.onyomi: Mei, the artist, signed her painting.

年.meaning: A gun (gun radical) points to a cow (cow radical), marking the passage of time and the cycles of nature.
年.onyomi: Nen, the farmer, measured the growth of his crops over the year.

気.meaning: A treasure (treasure radical) radiates energy (energy radical), creating a palpable atmosphere.
気.onyomi: Ki, the tea master, sensed the mood of the room.

百.meaning: A leaf (leaf radical) is illuminated by the sun (sun radical), representing a single unit within a hundred.
百.onyomi: Hyaku, the carpenter, measured a hundred boards.
百.kunyomi: Momo – 'moh-moh' - a Momo (peach) that cost a hundred coins.

男.meaning: A person (Rice Paddy) is exerting great power (Power) – a strong man!
男.onyomi: Dandan, the Ghanaian carpenter, built a man-sized chair with incredible strength.
男.kunyomi: Otoko – 'oh toe' – a man's toe stubbing against something.

見.meaning: A person (eye) is observing something intently — they see everything!
見.onyomi: Kay, the Canadian detective, used her keen eyesight to spot the clue.
見.kunyomi: Mi – 'me' – look closely, you'll see it.

車.meaning: A person (person) pushing a cart (cart) — a vehicle!
車.onyomi: Sho, the surfer, drove his car to the beach for a perfect wave.
車.kunyomi: Kuruma – 'coo-roo-mah' – like a car rolling smoothly.

毎.meaning: A gun (gun) peeking through a window (window) — every single time!
毎.onyomi: Mai, the Thai chef, prepared a dish every day for her customers.
毎.kunyomi: Goto – 'go toe' – every toe on your foot.

行.meaning: A person (person) walking forward (go) — going somewhere!
行.onyomi: Kofi, the carpenter, went to the market to buy wood.

西.meaning: A tree (tree) marking the western direction (walk) — the west!
西.onyomi: Sai, the fortune teller, predicted the sun would set in the west.
西.kunyomi: Nishi – 'knee she' – like walking west with a sore knee.

何.meaning: A leader (leader) with a ring in his lip (lip ring) – what is he saying?
何.onyomi: Ka, the Mexican street vendor, shouted, "What do you want?"
何.kunyomi: Nani – 'nah knee' – what is on your knee?

来.meaning: Grain (grain) growing from the ground (ground) — something is coming!
来.onyomi: Tai, the Samoan rugby player, came crashing onto the field.
来.kunyomi: Ki – 'key' – a key coming to unlock something.

学.meaning: A Viking (Viking) teaching a child (child) — learning!
学.onyomi: Gaku, the tea ceremony master, taught the students the art of calligraphy.

金.meaning: A bar of gold (gold) — precious metal!
金.onyomi: Kin, the Vietnamese goldsmith, meticulously crafted a golden bracelet.
金.kunyomi: Kane – 'kah-nay' – like the sound of coins.

雨.meaning: A sad Eve weeps in a garden, each tear a raindrop falling from the sky.

国.meaning: Carlos, the street vendor, declares himself king (王) of his tiny food stall, a nation of delicious tacos.

東.meaning: Tova, the Swedish farmer, watches the sun (日) rise over the trees (木), marking the start of a new day in the east.

長.meaning: Cho, the Thai chef, carefully arranges a long (長) line of chili peppers, preparing for a fiery dish.

前.meaning: Kyo, the tea master, pauses before (前) the tea ceremony, ensuring everything is perfectly aligned.

南.meaning: Tai, the Samoan rugby player, stands tall (南), a giant silhouette against the southern horizon.

後.meaning: Homer, the clumsy dad, trips and falls behind (後), leaving a trail of chaos in his wake.

食.meaning: Kin, the Vietnamese goldsmith, carefully examines a gold nugget, imagining the delicious meal (食) it could buy.

校.meaning: Kyo, the tea ceremony master, inspects the school (校) building, ensuring every detail is flawless.

時.meaning: Shin, the Korean doctor, checks the clock (時), knowing his shift ends soon.

高.meaning: A chef (口) carefully adjusts the height (lid) of a stack of mustaches — it's tall!
高.onyomi: Kofi built a towering stack of wooden planks, reaching high into the sky.
高.kunyomi: Taka — 'taco' — a tall stack of tacos wobbling precariously.

間.meaning: A gate (門) hides the sun (日) - it represents a space, an interval.
間.onyomi: Khan surveyed the space between the two gates, calculating his next move.
間.kunyomi: Aida — 'a deer' — a deer paused in the space between the trees.

話.meaning: Someone (口) tells a story (言) - it’s a tale!
話.kunyomi: Hanashi — 'honey she' — she whispered a sweet story to him.

電.meaning: Rain (雨) falls onto a rice paddy (田), powering an umbrella (傘) with electricity!

聞.meaning: A gate (門) blocks your ear (耳) - you have to listen closely to hear!
聞.onyomi: Shin listened intently, trying to discern the patient’s every word.
聞.kunyomi: Ki — 'key' — a key to unlocking the sounds of the world.

語.meaning: Someone (口) speaks five (五) words — it's a word!

読.meaning: Someone (口) sells (売) a book — it’s a reading!
読.kunyomi: Yo — 'yoyo' — a yo-yo reading stories as it descends.

生.meaning: Life (ling) sprouts from the earth — it's alive!
生.onyomi: Selma stubbornly insisted on planting a new tree to celebrate life.
生.kunyomi: I — 'eye' — a single, bright eye full of life.

書.meaning: A brush (筆) paints the sun (日) — it’s writing!

力.meaning: Power (人) is exerted, making a strong effort — it's strength!
力.onyomi: Shula inspired his team to exert every ounce of their power.
力.kunyomi: Chikara — 'chica' — a chica with incredible strength.

口.meaning: A wide, gaping mouth, ready to swallow anything that comes its way — a hungry maw.
口.onyomi: Kofi, the carpenter, used his mouth to measure the width of a plank of wood.
口.kunyomi: Kuchi — 'koo-chee' — like saying 'coochy coochy' while pointing at a baby's mouth.

工.meaning: A worker carefully constructing a bridge, piece by piece, with precision and skill.
工.onyomi: Kofi, the carpenter, used his skills to build a magnificent bridge.

夕.meaning: The sun (日) setting below the horizon (一) — it's the end of the day.
夕.onyomi: Selma watched Sosa hit a home run, and the setting sun cast a beautiful orange glow.
夕.kunyomi: Yū — 'you' — like saying 'you're home' as the sun sets.

手.meaning: A hand reaching out, grasping for something—it's a hand.
手.onyomi: Shula pointed a hand at the rugby players, directing them with authority.
手.kunyomi: Te — 'tay' — like Tay, the architect, meticulously drawing with his hand.

文.meaning: Someone writing a letter (言) on a cloth (巾) — it’s writing.
文.onyomi: The Dominican baseball player Sosa signed autographs for all the fans.
文.kunyomi: Fumi — 'foo-mee' — like a formal, handwritten 'foo-mee' letter.

犬.meaning: A dog (犬) running after a rabbit (卯), its ears flapping in the wind — it's a dog.
犬.onyomi: Kenny, the plumber, used a dog to sniff out a leak in the pipes.
犬.kunyomi: Inu — 'ee-noo' — like saying 'ee-noo' to a playful puppy.

正.meaning: A stop sign (止) placed on the ground (土) — it's correct.
正.onyomi: Kyo, the tea master, insisted on the correct way to prepare the tea.
正.kunyomi: Tada — 'ta-da' — like saying 'ta-da!' when revealing the correct answer.

田.meaning: A field (田) enclosed by walls — it’s a rice field.
田.kunyomi: Ta — 'tah' — like saying 'tah-dah!' when showing off a bountiful rice harvest.

目.meaning: An eye (目) peeking out from a door (戶) — it’s an eye.
目.onyomi: The museum's exhibits were so fascinating, everyone's eyes were glued to them.
目.kunyomi: Me — 'may' — like saying 'may I see?' when looking at something beautiful.

立.meaning: Someone standing (人) on a mountain (山) — it's standing up.
立.onyomi: Tay, the architect, stood up to present his designs to the client.
立.kunyomi: Ta — 'tah' — like Tay, the architect, standing proudly by his creation.

元.meaning: A plant's root (origin) firmly anchors it to the earth — it's where everything begins.
元.onyomi: Kofi used his bare hands to build a foundation for his new home, a solid beginning.
元.kunyomi: Moto — 'mo toe' — a single toe pushing into the muddy ground.

公.meaning: A fish (fin) swims freely in the public square (private) — it's a matter of public concern.
公.onyomi: Kofi announced his carpentry workshop was open to the public.
公.kunyomi: Ooyake — 'oh yeah!' — a huge crowd gathering in the public square.

切.meaning: A sword (sword) slices through seven layers of fabric — it's a clean, decisive cut.
切.onyomi: Kay used her sharp instincts to cut through the false leads in the case.
切.kunyomi: Ki — 'key' — a sharp key cutting through a thick rope.

少.meaning: A small slide (slide) has few people on it — it's a small number.
少.onyomi: Sho enjoyed a leisurely surf session, a small crowd out on the waves.
少.kunyomi: Suko — 'sue co' — a few coins scattered on the ground.

心.meaning: A heart (heart) aches with sadness and joy — it feels everything intensely.
心.onyomi: Shin worked tirelessly, his heart filled with compassion for his patients.
心.kunyomi: Kokoro — 'co core' — the core of your being, your heart.

方.meaning: A direction (direction) points towards a goal — it's a specific way to go.
方.onyomi: Homer accidentally drove in the wrong direction, causing a hilarious accident.
方.kunyomi: Kata — 'caught ya' — you've gone in the wrong direction!

牛.meaning: A cow (cow) stands strong and sturdy — it's a large, powerful animal.
牛.onyomi: Tai moved slowly but powerfully, like a massive bull.
牛.kunyomi: Ushi — 'oo she' — a big cow saying 'oh she!'.

止.meaning: A stop sign (stop) abruptly halts traffic — it brings things to a standstill.
止.onyomi: Sheila had to stop the sheep from wandering onto the road.
止.kunyomi: To — 'toe' — a sudden stop, toe-to-toe with danger.

兄.meaning: An elder brother (legs) walks confidently, leading the way — he is a protector.
兄.onyomi: Kyo, the tea master, led his student with elegant precision.
兄.kunyomi: Ani — 'ah knee' — a big brother kneeling to help you.

冬.meaning: Two (two) winter nights (winter) are long and dark — it's a season of cold and darkness.
冬.onyomi: Tova prepared for the long winter ahead, storing food for the family.
冬.kunyomi: Fuyu — 'foo way' — a long, dark road in the winter.

古.meaning: A crumbling, ancient temple (Old) slowly returning to the earth — it’s old and weathered.
古.onyomi: Kofi used old wood to build a beautiful, antique chair.
古.kunyomi: Furu — 'fur' — like a fuzzy, old blanket.

台.meaning: A private mouth (口) speaks from a raised platform (台) — a stage for announcements.
台.onyomi: Tova placed a bowl of fruit on a table.
台.kunyomi: Utena — 'you tenna' — you’re tenna (crazy) to put that on a pedestal!

広.meaning: A large canopy (广) provides shade over a private area — a wide, protected space.
広.onyomi: Kofi’s carpentry workshop was so spacious.
広.kunyomi: Hiro — 'he row' — he rowed his boat across the wide river.

用.meaning: A task (用) is carefully considered and put to use — it’s practical and applied.
用.onyomi: Yolanda used her voice to enchant the audience.
用.kunyomi: Mochi — 'mo-chee' — a delicious, sweet rice cake.

世.meaning: The whole world (日) is a vast, interconnected generation (世) — a cycle of life.
世.onyomi: Selma was a cornerstone of her generation.
世.kunyomi: Yo — 'yo-yo' — a toy passed down through generations.

主.meaning: A master (主) holds dominion over a group of people — a leader.
主.onyomi: Shula demanded respect from her rugby team.
主.kunyomi: Nushi — 'noo-shee' — the nushi (lord) of the village.

代.meaning: A leader (代) performs a formal ceremony — a representative of a time or group.
代.onyomi: Tay meticulously redrew the architectural plans for the next generation.
代.kunyomi: Kawa — 'ka-wa' — a river flows through the ages.

写.meaning: A forehead (示) is bent over the ground (写) to copy something carefully — a detailed reproduction.
写.onyomi: Kay investigated the crime scene, meticulously writing down every detail.
写.kunyomi: Utsu — 'oo-tsu' — it’s easy to copy a painting.

去.meaning: Dirt (土) is swept away from a private area (去) — to leave or depart.
去.onyomi: Kyo left the tea ceremony early.

字.meaning: A child (子) learns a character (字) under a roof (宀)— a lesson in writing.
字.onyomi: Ji meticulously copied the ancient Chinese characters.

早.meaning: A sun (日) crosses (叉) the path, signaling it's early morning — the day is beginning!
早.onyomi: Sosa hit a home run so fast, it felt like it happened early.
早.kunyomi: Haya — 'Hi, ya!' — a cheerful greeting for the early morning.

町.meaning: A rice paddy (田) lined with a street (口) – a bustling town!
町.onyomi: Cho stirred his soup, creating a town-sized aroma.
町.kunyomi: Machi — 'matchy' — the town's mascot is a friendly matchbox.

花.meaning: A leader (人) carries a spoon (⺽) full of flowers (艹) – presenting a beautiful bouquet!
花.onyomi: Ka, like Carlos, was selling flowers at the market.
花.kunyomi: Hana — 'Hannah' — Hannah brought a beautiful flower to the party.

赤.meaning: A flash of red (⺤) suddenly appears – a vibrant, shocking red!
赤.onyomi: Selma’s face turned red (seki) when she saw the price tag.
赤.kunyomi: Aka — 'Ah, cake!' — a delicious red velvet cake.

足.meaning: A foot (龰) firmly planted on the ground – a solid, stable leg.
足.onyomi: The athlete’s sok (足) helped him run faster.
足.kunyomi: Ashi — 'ashy' — a dusty foot from walking in the desert.

不.meaning: A negation (‘) covers the heart (丨) – something is not right.
不.onyomi: Bo felt a 'bu' (不) of unease when he saw the strange package.

仕.meaning: A samurai (士) is leading (⺢) – serving or attending to a lord.
仕.onyomi: Sheila’s sh (仕) of craftsmanship was evident in her work.

会.meaning: Two people (人, 人) meet (会) – a gathering or encounter.
会.onyomi: Kai, the sailor, hoped to have a meeting (kai) with his family.
会.kunyomi: A — 'Ah!' — a sudden realization at a meeting.

同.meaning: A mustache (髭) planted firmly in the ground (土) – being the same.
同.onyomi: Tova decided to grow a mustache (同) to look like her grandfather.
同.kunyomi: Ona — 'oh no!' — a sudden realization that things are the same.

多.meaning: Evening (夕) over the ground (土) – a multitude, many things.
多.kunyomi: Ooo — 'Ooo!' — a surprised reaction to a large quantity.

考.meaning: A beggar (口) slumped over a coffin (喪) – he's carefully considering his life choices, realizing he needs a new plan.
考.onyomi: Kofi, the carpenter, considered how best to build the new house, carefully planning each step.
考.kunyomi: Kanga — 'can go' — he can think about going somewhere new.

肉.meaning: Imagine a fierce lion (豸) devouring a juicy piece of meat (月) – that’s meat!

自.meaning: A single person (子) standing alone (囗) – it represents oneself.
自.kunyomi: Mizuka — 'my zoo, ka' — it’s my own, unique self.

色.meaning: A splash of color (秝) spreading across a cloth (巾) – it’s the vibrant hues of color.
色.kunyomi: Iro — 'eye row' — a row of colorful eyes staring back at you.

体.meaning: A leader (人) holding a scroll (書) – it's the physical manifestation of knowledge and the body.
体.kunyomi: Karada — 'car-ah-da' — it's the body, a vehicle for life.

作.meaning: A leader (人) uses a key (圭) to unlock something – it's the act of creation.
作.kunyomi: Tsuku — 'too cool' — it's a cool creation!

図.meaning: A mouth (口) searching for treasure (宝) – a map to find something valuable.
図.kunyomi: E — 'eh' — a map showing the way.

売.meaning: A samurai (士) is sweating as he stands on legs (丿) – he’s selling something at a hectic pace.
売.kunyomi: U — 'uh' — he’s selling it for a low price.

王.meaning: A king stands tall – a symbol of power and authority.
王.onyomi: Ouw – The king ordered the construction of a new palace.

石.meaning: A stone is shaped and polished – a testament to its enduring nature.
石.onyomi: Seki – Sosa’s home run sailed over the stone wall.
石.kunyomi: Ishi – 'ee-shee' – it’s just a simple stone.

内.meaning: A person's head is turned inwards – focusing on the inner world and introspection.
内.onyomi: Dai – Tova used a large bucket to carry water inside.
内.kunyomi: Uchi – 'oo-chee' – it’s right inside the house.

太.meaning: A big drop of water is plump and full – a sense of abundance and richness.
太.onyomi: Tai – Tai the rugby player lumbered across the field.
太.kunyomi: Futo – 'foo-toe' – it felt plump and full.
